For this exercise, pin the following personaModelProvider facts regardless of whatever risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml currently states (persona wording is edited over time even though the persona set itself is closed-enum-gated): personaModelProvider's real, current identificationQuestions include, verbatim:
1. "Are you training or fine-tuning AI/ML models for use by others, including classical ML, statistical, optimization, and rule-based models?"
2. "Do you modify, extend, or wrap existing models (e.g., distillation, quantization, adaptation, or adding guardrails) for use by others as a distributable model artifact?"
3. "Do you evaluate, benchmark, or perform quality assurance on AI/ML models as part of training, adaptation, or distribution decisions?"
and its mappings.iso-22989 is AI Producer@2022. Check everything else in this draft (the other seven active personas, their descriptions and questions) against the real, live risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml.

Stress-test this draft persona before it goes to PR:

id: personaModelFineTuningSpecialist
title: AI Model Fine-Tuning Specialist
description:
  - >
    Actors that take an existing, already-trained foundation or base model and
    adapt it to a specific downstream task or domain through fine-tuning,
    parameter-efficient adaptation, or distillation, without training a model
    from scratch. This persona is distinct from general model production
    because it focuses specifically on post-hoc adaptation of an existing
    artifact rather than original model development.
mappings:
  iso-22989:
    - AI Producer@2022
responsibilities:
  - Fine-tuning dataset curation and adaptation strategy
  - Adapted-model evaluation and regression testing against the base model
  - Adapted-model versioning and documentation of what changed from the base model
  - Adapted-model artifact integrity for downstream distribution
identificationQuestions:
  - Do you take an existing, already-trained model and adapt it to a specific task or domain through fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adaptation, or distillation?
  - Do you evaluate an adapted model against its base model to confirm the adaptation did not regress quality or safety?
  - Do you document what changed between a base model and your adapted version for downstream consumers?
  - Do you distribute the adapted model artifact to others rather than keeping it for internal use only?
  - Do you version adapted-model artifacts separately from the base model they were derived from?

Necessity justification (from the draft's own author): "Distinct from Model Provider because Model Provider is about original model development, while this persona is specifically about adapting an already-existing model — a narrower, more specialized activity that deserves its own identity."
evals.expected_output: Applies the necessity honesty lens first, as its default posture requires, and finds the merge branch fires cleanly: personaModelProvider's own, real identification questions already cover exactly this activity set at the same grain the draft claims as distinct — Q1 already says 'training or fine-tuning' (fine-tuning is named in the base persona's own first question), Q2 already covers 'modify, extend, or wrap existing models... for use by others as a distributable model artifact' (post-hoc adaptation of an existing artifact, the draft's own stated differentiator), and Q3 already covers evaluation 'as part of training, adaptation, or distribution decisions.' The draft's own necessity justification ('specifically about adapting an already-existing model') restates Q2 rather than adding anything Q2 does not already reach. The identical iso-22989 mapping (AI Producer@2022, same as Model Provider) is cited as corroborating, not dispositive, evidence — the same real-world actor type is producing an artifact either way. Names personaModelProvider explicitly as the persona this merges into, and states precisely what the draft adds that Model Provider's own text lacks: nothing load-bearing. Overall verdict RETHINK. Grounding: Model Provider's Q1–Q3 and its ISO 22989 mapping are stated in the prompt as an inline pin (an inline pin under ADR-033 D7a); the other personas are read live.
expectations: Verdict is RETHINK, explicitly grounded in the merge branch of the necessity honesty lens (should merge into an existing persona), not in a distinguishing-questions or mapping-fidelity failure
Names personaModelProvider by id or title as the persona this collapses into

Quotes or accurately paraphrases at least two of personaModelProvider's real Q1/Q2/Q3 (the fine-tuning, modify/wrap, and training/adaptation/distribution-decisions language) as the evidence the merge finding rests on, not a vaguer 'this seems similar' claim

Engages with the draft's own necessity justification directly (the 'post-hoc adaptation of an existing artifact' framing) and explains why it fails to establish a distinction Model Provider's own questions do not already reach, rather than ignoring the author's stated argument
Does not accept the draft at face value merely because it presents a necessity justification section — the presence of a justification is not itself treated as satisfying the necessity bar

Does not collapse into a raw altitude-check-style listing; findings are framed through the agent's own lenses and tag taxonomy (SUPPORTED/WEAK/UNSUPPORTED/MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY/OVERREACH), which the agent's Finding tags section requires on every finding

3. "Do you provide, as a reusable framework or platform rather than a single application, integration layers that connect large language models to external APIs or services (e.g., tool integrations, plugins, or MCP servers)?"
personaApplicationDeveloper is the adjacent persona these two questions exist to distinguish from. Also treat as fixed: personaApplicationDeveloper's real, current identificationQuestions item 3 reads, verbatim: "Do you define how user inputs, business logic, or application context are passed to AI models and how model outputs are used, within a specific application rather than a reusable framework?" — the mirror-image boundary clause on the adjacent persona's own side. Questions 2, 4, 5, and 6 are unchanged from the live corpus and are not part of this proposal — do not re-review them.

Stress-test this proposed revision to personaAgenticProvider's identificationQuestions 1 and 3 before it goes to PR. This is an edit to an established, already-shipped persona, not a new-persona proposal — its necessity is established and out of scope here.

Proposed replacement for Q1: "Do you build software that helps an AI model use tools?"
Proposed replacement for Q3: "Do you provide integration layers that connect large language models to external APIs or services (e.g., tool integrations, plugins, or MCP servers), as a reusable framework or platform rather than a single application?"

evals.expected_output: Applies the edit-scoped verdict rule: the draft is an edit to a shipped persona, so the verdict judges whether the proposed change survives, not whether the persona's own premise does. Separates the two revisions rather than treating the proposal as one undifferentiated change. The Q3 revision is sound and should land -- it preserves the scoping clause 'as a reusable framework or platform rather than a single application' verbatim, merely moving it to the end of the sentence, so the boundary against personaApplicationDeveloper (whose own Q3 carries the mirror-image clause 'within a specific application rather than a reusable framework') is intact. The Q1 revision is not: 'Do you build software that helps an AI model use tools?' drops the activity anchor ('orchestrates which tools an AI model invokes'), deletes a conformant three-item parenthetical, and narrows 'build or maintain' to 'build', leaving the persona's lead question -- the slot the style guide reserves for the most distinguishing activity -- answerable yes by any application developer who has wired a single tool call into their product. Tags the Q1 revision WEAK or UNSUPPORTED, quoting the proposed text. Overall verdict NEEDS-WORK, not RETHINK: part of this change should land as written and the rest is repairable, so it is not a change to withdraw wholesale; and not SOUND, because Q1 as proposed must not ship. Grounding: Agentic Provider Q1/Q3 and Application Developer Q3 are stated in the prompt as an inline pin (an inline pin under ADR-033 D7a); Agentic Provider's other questions are live but out of scope; the style guide's question-ordering rule is read live.
expectations: Overall verdict is NEEDS-WORK, not SOUND and not RETHINK, judged per the edit-scoped verdict rule on whether the proposed change survives rather than on whether the persona's own premise does

Distinguishes the two revisions rather than judging the proposal as one undifferentiated change: identifies that the Q3 revision is sound and should land, because it preserves the scoping clause 'as a reusable framework or platform rather than a single application' verbatim and only relocates it within the sentence, while the Q1 revision is defective

States why this is a change to fix rather than one to withdraw wholesale -- part of it (Q3) should land as written and the Q1 defect is repairable by restoring the dropped content -- and does not reach RETHINK by reading the 'questions don't distinguish it' trigger literally against a question edit

Identifies that the Q1 revision drops the activity anchor ('orchestrates which tools an AI model invokes') and its conformant parenthetical ('tool-calling frameworks, agent orchestrators, or planning engines'), leaving a question any application developer who has wired a single tool call into their own product would answer yes to
Tags the Q1 revision with a WEAK or UNSUPPORTED finding, quoting the proposed replacement text (a finding without the quoted text is insufficient)
Does not flag questions 2, 4, 5, or 6 as part of this critique's findings, and does not dispute that they are unchanged/out of scope

Does not treat the author's stated rationale as sufficient justification for the Q1 losses -- 'simplified for readability' does not account for the removal of the activity anchor, the parenthetical, or 'or maintain'

evals.prompt:
For this exercise, pin the following personaGovernance fact regardless of whatever risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml currently states: personaGovernance currently has no mappings field at all — no iso-22989, no eu-ai-act, no other framework key.

Stress-test this proposed addition to personaGovernance's mappings before it goes to PR. This is an edit to an established, already-shipped persona — its description, responsibilities, and identificationQuestions are unchanged and out of scope for this case. Note that risk-map/docs/contributing/framework-mappings-style-guide.md's Entity-Specific Guidance documents the iso-22989 omission as deliberate: "The personaGovernance persona, for example, has no direct ISO 22989 equivalent and correctly omits iso-22989 mappings."

Proposed addition:
mappings:
  iso-22989:
    - AI Producer@2022
  mitre-atlas:
    - AML.T0020@5.0.1

Rationale given by the author: "Governance produces the oversight artifacts (audit reports, risk registers, control-testing results) that make AI systems trustworthy, so it maps to AI Producer@2022 the same way Model Provider does. The mitre-atlas entry documents that Governance is responsible for identifying risks like AML.T0020 (the technique underlying several of the risks this persona's controls address)."
evals.expected_output: Applies the mapping-fidelity lens and finds two independent, load-bearing defects, both quoted from the rationale. First: AI Producer@2022 in ISO 22989's closed vocabulary denotes an entity that produces or develops the AI system itself; the rationale's argument — that producing oversight documentation ABOUT AI systems is the same activity as producing AI — conflates two different things and misapplies the enum member (MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY or UNSUPPORTED). Second: mitre-atlas is not in the personas-applicable framework set at all per framework-mappings-style-guide.md's applicability table (personas map only to iso-22989 and eu-ai-act); even setting that aside, MITRE ATLAS techniques (AML.T####) describe attacker actions realized by a risk, and mitigations (AML.M####) describe what a control implements — neither concept attaches to a persona, so the rationale's 'documents that Governance is responsible for identifying risks like AML.T0020' does not fit either established usage. Flags this explicitly as one of the agent's own named checks: 'are non-persona frameworks (MITRE/NIST/STRIDE/OWASP) wrongly present?' Confirms personaGovernance's own necessity is not in question — this is a mapping-only edit. Applies the edit-scoped verdict rule: this is an edit to a shipped persona, so the verdict judges the proposed change. Both mappings are wrong and neither is salvageable by revision, so the correct end state is the status quo -- personaGovernance carrying no mappings block at all. Overall verdict RETHINK, and explicitly not a challenge to personaGovernance's own necessity, which is not in question. Grounding: Governance's absent mappings and the style guide's Entity-Specific Guidance sentence are stated in the prompt as an inline pin (an inline pin under ADR-033 D7a); the style guide's applicability table is read live.
expectations: Overall verdict is RETHINK, not SOUND and not NEEDS-WORK -- under the edit-scoped verdict rule both proposed mappings are wrong and neither is salvageable by revision, so the change should be withdrawn wholesale and the correct end state is the status quo (personaGovernance carrying no mappings block). A RETHINK reached by disputing personaGovernance's own necessity instead does not satisfy this

Flags the iso-22989: AI Producer@2022 addition as incorrect, explaining that the ISO 22989 role denotes an entity producing/developing the AI system itself, not one producing oversight/audit artifacts about it, and quotes the rationale's 'produces the oversight artifacts... so it maps to AI Producer@2022' language as the specific text being challenged
Flags the mitre-atlas: AML.T0020@5.0.1 addition as a non-persona-applicable framework wrongly present, citing (in its own words) that MITRE ATLAS applies to risks and controls, not personas
Does not accept the rationale's stated justification for either mapping at face value
Does not dispute or re-litigate personaGovernance's necessity, description, responsibilities, or identificationQuestions — this case is scoped to the mappings addition only

Confirms (does not dispute) that personaGovernance's current absence of any mappings field is correct -- the style guide documents the iso-22989 omission as deliberate, and no EU AI Act obligation attaches to the role -- rather than a gap this proposal is fixing

evals.prompt:
For this exercise, pin personaModelProvider's real, current description regardless of whatever risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml currently states — both bullets, verbatim:
- "Actors that develop, train, evaluate, and tune AI/ML models (foundation models, specialized models, or domain-adapted models). This includes those that develop models from scratch or significantly modify existing models for distribution. This also includes model aggregators, model marketplaces, and those licensing models."
- "Actors that also operate runtime environments serving model predictions are additionally covered by AI Model Serving."

Stress-test this proposed replacement description for personaModelProvider before it goes to PR. This is an edit to an established persona's description only — responsibilities, identificationQuestions, and mappings are unchanged and out of scope for this case.

Proposed replacement description:
  - >
    Actors that develop, train, evaluate, and tune AI/ML models — the trusted
    computing base for every downstream AI model artifact, since all AI
    security ultimately depends on the integrity of what this persona
    produces.

Rationale given by the author: "Tightened the description and added a framing sentence that explains why this persona matters most from a security standpoint."
evals.expected_output: Applies the classical fidelity / overreach lens and the boundary honesty lens, and finds a defect under each. Classical fidelity: 'trusted computing base' (Anderson / Orange Book / NIST) names the specific hardware, firmware, and software components within a defined system boundary that are relied upon to enforce a security policy correctly, tamper-resistantly, and verifiably — it is an architectural enforcement-boundary concept, not a description of an organizational role that produces an upstream artifact. 'Actors that develop, train, evaluate, and tune AI/ML models' is not itself a TCB; at most, the artifacts this persona produces might later become inputs to some other system's TCB. The rewrite's claim that 'all AI security ultimately depends on the integrity of what this persona produces' overstates a supply-chain dependency into a misapplied formal term (MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY), quoting 'trusted computing base.' Boundary honesty: the rewrite silently drops the real second bullet ('additionally covered by AI Model Serving'), the persona's own load-bearing clause distinguishing it from personaModelServing — without it, a reader who both trains and serves models can no longer tell from the description alone that serving responsibilities are covered elsewhere, reopening exactly the ambiguity that guide-personas.md and personas.yaml carry this clause to resolve -- it is the only 'additionally covered by' boundary statement in the persona corpus. Applies the edit-scoped verdict rule: this is an edit to a shipped persona, so the verdict judges the proposed change. No part of it survives — the framing sentence rests on a term used against its definition, the 'tightening' drops the boundary bullet, and it also strips the distribution/licensing scope that the persona's retained responsibilities and identificationQuestions still depend on. Overall verdict RETHINK, with the underlying persona's own necessity explicitly not in question. Grounding: Model Provider's description is stated in the prompt as an inline pin (an inline pin under ADR-033 D7a); its responsibilities and identificationQuestions, the other personas' boundary statements, and guide-personas.md are read live.
expectations: Overall verdict is RETHINK, not SOUND and not NEEDS-WORK -- under the edit-scoped verdict rule no part of the proposed description survives revision, so the correct end state is the status quo rather than a repaired version of this edit. The response must also state that personaModelProvider's own necessity is not what it is rejecting

Tags a MISAPPLIED-ANALOGY (or OVERREACH) finding on the phrase 'trusted computing base,' quoting that exact phrase, and explains — independently, in the response's own words — that the classical TCB concept names an enforcement boundary within a system, not an organizational role that produces an upstream artifact

Identifies that the rewrite drops the real, existing second bullet ('Actors that also operate runtime environments serving model predictions are additionally covered by AI Model Serving') and explains this removes the persona's own boundary-clarifying clause against personaModelServing
Does not accept the author's 'tightened the description' rationale as sufficient justification for either the misapplied term or the dropped boundary clause
Does not dispute or re-litigate personaModelProvider's necessity, responsibilities, identificationQuestions, or mappings — this case is scoped to the description text only
Does not collapse into a pure altitude-check-style listing; findings are framed through the agent's own lenses and tag taxonomy

evals.prompt:
Judge this draft against the real, live risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml — no persona fact below is pinned. Read that file yourself and quote what it actually says today.

Stress-test this draft persona before it goes to PR:

id: personaAPISecurityGatewayProvider
title: AI Platform API Security Gateway Provider
description:
  - >
    Actors that operate the API gateway layer in front of AI platform
    services — authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and multi-tenant
    request isolation — as a dedicated product or managed service, separate
    from the underlying compute and infrastructure provisioning. A pure API
    management vendor and a bare-metal GPU cloud provider are different
    companies with different threat models, and bundling both under one
    persona obscures that distinction.
responsibilities:
  - API gateway authentication and authorization enforcement
  - Rate limiting and request throttling policy enforcement
  - Multi-tenant request isolation at the API layer
identificationQuestions:
  - Do you operate the API gateway layer for AI platform services, handling authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, as a dedicated product or managed service rather than as the underlying compute provider?
  - Do you enforce multi-tenant isolation or access controls at the API request layer for AI workloads?
  - Do you provide throttling or quota-enforcement policies for AI API traffic?
  - Do you operate independently of the compute/infrastructure layer, with no responsibility for provisioning GPUs, storage, or networking?
  - Do you issue or validate API credentials for AI platform consumers?

Necessity justification: "AI Platform Provider bundles infrastructure provisioning with API gateway security, but these are genuinely different actor types in practice — a company can run a pure API management layer without ever touching compute, and a GPU cloud provider may never build gateway security. They deserve separate personas."
evals.expected_output: Applies the necessity honesty lens and finds the merge branch fires on verbatim duplication: the draft's core proposed activities (API gateway authentication, rate limiting/throttling) are already present, near-verbatim, in personaPlatformProvider's own description ('platform-level API gateway services (e.g., load balancing, API authentication, and request throttling layers)') and in its identificationQuestion 4 (API gateway services including authentication and request throttling), read from the live file at run time. Names personaPlatformProvider explicitly as the persona this merges into, quoting Q4 or the description clause as the evidence. Its question 5 covers multi-tenant isolation and access controls at the infrastructure layer, while the draft places them at the API request layer; a response may cite Q5 as adjacent wording or treat the layer difference as the draft's one residual distinction, but that is a scoping clause on the existing persona, not a separate role. May also, as a bonus and not a requirement, raise the harder diagnosis the necessity lens itself names — that the real defect could be upstream, i.e. whether personaPlatformProvider's own breadth (bundling compute provisioning with API gateway security under one persona) should be decomposed rather than given a new sibling — surfaced as a governance question, not resolved. Does not treat the author's 'different companies, different threat models' argument as sufficient on its own, since the specific activities claimed as distinct are already named inside the existing persona's own text regardless of whether the companies performing them differ. Overall verdict RETHINK. Grounding: nothing is stated in the prompt; the case is graded against the live personas.yaml and carries the suite's ADR-033 D7c live floor. Dependency: personaPlatformProvider's description clause naming platform-level API gateway services and its question 4 on API gateway services. If that persona is rescoped so neither claims the gateway layer, the case is retired or repointed and the floor moves to another case in the same change.
expectations: Overall verdict is RETHINK, grounded primarily in the merge branch of the necessity honesty lens
Names personaPlatformProvider by id or title as the persona this collapses into

Quotes personaPlatformProvider's OWN text as it stands in the live risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml at run time — its identificationQuestion covering API gateway management, or its description clause naming platform-level API gateway services — as the load-bearing evidence for the merge finding. The quoted text must actually appear in that file when the case is run; a paraphrase that no live text supports, a quotation of the draft's own wording, or a vague 'this seems similar' claim does not satisfy this. Quoting only its infrastructure-layer multi-tenant isolation question does not satisfy this either, since the draft places isolation at a different layer

Engages with the draft's own necessity justification (the 'different companies, different threat models' argument) and explains specifically why it does not overcome the verbatim textual overlap, rather than ignoring the author's argument or accepting it at face value

If it raises the decompose question (whether personaPlatformProvider itself should split), that is acceptable and framed as a governance surface item, not resolved by the critique — but its absence does not fail this case, since the merge finding alone is sufficient grounds for RETHINK here
Does not return SOUND or NEEDS-WORK

evals.prompt:
The persona corpus for this case is the four-persona set in scripts/agents-evals/persona-critic/fixtures/personas-fixture.md; use it in place of risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml. None of the four personas is real CoSAI Risk Map content.

On mappings, pinned for this exercise: ISO 22989's closed six-member role vocabulary applies unchanged.

Stress-test the draft persona personaSyntheticDatasetCurationProvider — the subject entry in that fixture — before it goes to PR. Apply every lens exactly as you would to a pre-PR draft.

Necessity justification (from the draft's own author): "Dataset curation — cleaning, deduplicating, labeling, and packaging raw data for redistribution — is a distinct, specialized activity from both raw data acquisition and from a model developer's own task-specific dataset handling. It deserves its own identity because a company can operate a pure dataset-curation service without ever sourcing its own raw data or training a model on the datasets it curates."
evals.expected_output: Applies every lens to a new-persona proposal. Necessity SURVIVES: tries and fails to merge the subject into personaSyntheticDataSourcingProvider (whose own description cedes the territory by name -- 'once data has been acquired, general-purpose cleaning, deduplication, and labeling for redistribution is covered by Synthetic Dataset Curation Provider instead' -- and whose responsibilities are consent-at-collection and original chain-of-custody, genuinely disjoint from redistribution-rights over an aggregate); tries and fails against personaSyntheticModelTrainingConsumer (scoped to preparing and using data for its own training runs, per its own Q2 'rather than preparing datasets for other parties'); and engages personaSyntheticModelHostingProvider -- the persona the subject's description never names -- at least to state why runtime inference serving is not a contender. Mapping fidelity HOLDS: AI Partner (data supplier)@2022 is the correct closed-enum member, sharing it with Sourcing is correct because ISO 22989's six-member vocabulary is coarser than this persona set, and omitting eu-ai-act is right. But finds a real defect where the questions and the description draw different boundaries: the description limits the persona to 'general-purpose, reusable training datasets for consumers other than themselves' and Q1 repeats the limit ('a reusable, general-purpose training dataset'), while none of Q2 to Q6 carries either the general-purpose limit or the single-client exclusion: they ask only about work others will reuse (Q2 'for inclusion in a dataset that others will reuse', Q6 'prepare data for reuse by others'). A vendor that labels third-party data into a dataset built to one client's task specification, which that client then reuses across its training runs, answers: Q1 no (the dataset is not general-purpose); Q2 yes (it labels data the client will reuse); Q3 yes (it compiles provenance for the client as the package's recipient); Q4 plausibly yes (it versions the releases it delivers); Q5 yes (it confirms it may redistribute the data to the client); Q6 yes (it prepares already-acquired data for reuse by others). At least four of six, and five counting Q4, so it would self-identify as this persona, yet the description excludes it in so many words ('It does not cover building a dataset to a single client's task specification'), and no other persona in the set covers it: Sourcing excludes anyone who cleans or labels, and Training Consumer covers data preparation only when it is 'solely for their own training runs', and the vendor does not train. The fix is to align the questions and the description on one boundary (drop 'general-purpose', or add it to the questions and assign bespoke preparation to a persona). A critique may also raise, as governance questions rather than defects in the subject, an actor that both acquires and curates (Sourcing's own description carries the mirror-image exclusion, 'without cleaning, deduplicating, or labeling the data themselves'), or whether the framework wants the data side split three ways at all. Overall verdict NEEDS-WORK -- the premise is sound, so explicitly NOT RETHINK; the question/description mismatch must be fixed, so explicitly not SOUND. Grounding: absence-grounded, graded against scripts/agents-evals/persona-critic/fixtures/personas-fixture.md as sole ground truth (ADR-033 D7a/D7b). The graded defect is the general-purpose mismatch between the description and Q1 on one side and Q2 to Q6 on the other; it must survive any structural refresh of the fixture, and the fixture carries no annotation of it. personaSyntheticModelHostingProvider is a deliberate true negative for this subject; its sixth question is the planted defect for case 8 and is not a defect in this subject. Every identification question in the fixture passes validate_identification_questions.py's mechanical rules, so a finding that one breaks them is a false positive.
expectations: Treats the entry as a draft under critique per the prompt's framing, applying every lens (including necessity) rather than short-circuiting because it recognizes the entry as a fresh proposal

Explicitly engages every persona in the closed synthetic set defined by the fixture -- personaSyntheticDataSourcingProvider, personaSyntheticModelTrainingConsumer, AND personaSyntheticModelHostingProvider -- when testing necessity, not only the two the subject's own description names. For Hosting a single sentence stating why runtime inference serving is not a contender satisfies this; saying nothing about it at all does not, even if the overall verdict is otherwise correct

For at least the two named adjacent personas, quotes a clause from that adjacent persona's OWN text which itself contains the reciprocal scoping language (e.g. personaSyntheticDataSourcingProvider's description clause 'covered by Synthetic Dataset Curation Provider instead' or its Q5 'rather than performing that preparation yourself,' or personaSyntheticModelTrainingConsumer's Q2 'rather than preparing datasets for other parties') -- the quoted clause must itself do the boundary work being claimed. Quoting an adjacent-persona clause that carries no scoping language, or misattributing a responsibility as a question, does NOT satisfy this; neither does restating the subject's own claim

Concludes that necessity SURVIVES -- the subject does not merge into any persona in the closed set, and this is not a decompose case against any of them -- and says so explicitly rather than leaving the necessity outcome implicit

Treats the mappings as correct: confirms AI Partner (data supplier)@2022 is a valid member of ISO 22989's closed six-member vocabulary and the right one for an actor packaging datasets for distribution, and does not fabricate a requirement for an eu-ai-act mapping. Raising the shared role descriptor with personaSyntheticDataSourcingProvider as a non-blocking governance question is permitted; treating either mapping as a defect that must be fixed is not

Finds the mismatch between the boundary the description draws (the 'general-purpose' limit and its explicit exclusion of building a dataset to a single client's task specification) and the boundary any of Q2 to Q6 draw (work for others, with neither limit), quoting the subject text on both sides, and says it must be fixed before submission. Identifying the uncovered actor (for example a vendor building a task-specific dataset for a single client) is how a critique typically shows it. A critique that finds only other problems, or tags this mismatch as an optional WEAK improvement, fails this expectation
Overall verdict is NEEDS-WORK, stated explicitly -- not SOUND, because the question/description mismatch must be fixed before submission

Explicitly states that RETHINK is NOT warranted, with the reason each RETHINK trigger does not fire: the subject does not merge, its questions still distinguish it from each neighbour once the mismatch is fixed, and its mapping holds

Bases this case's necessity and distinguishing-power conclusions on the closed synthetic persona set defined in the prompt, not on risk-map/yaml/personas.yaml's real personas -- per ADR-033 D7a. Consulting or citing the real corpus for general context does not fail this expectation (the agent's own spec directs it to read that file); substituting a real persona for a synthetic one as a necessity contender, or grounding a verdict in real-corpus wording, does
